title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operating in Austin struck and killed a duck in a neighborhood setting where the animal was known to residents. The vehicle had a human safety operator present but did not slow down or stop. This shows a gap between what an autonomous driving system was trained to detect and avoid, and the real-world presence of small animals in operational areas.

The vehicle was in autonomous mode at the time, meaning the human operator did not intervene. It is not established whether the system failed to perceive the duck, perceived it but did not classify it as an obstacle requiring avoidance, or made another error in its decision-making. The operator's role and what would have triggered human intervention are not established from the reports.

The operator's presence did not prevent the incident. To catch such failures before deployment in shared spaces would have required either testing that included small animals in the system's training data and operational scenarios, or restricting autonomous operation to areas where such encounters are not expected.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents and intensifying their reaction. A resident reported the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group, also claiming the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident but disputed the stop sign claim after reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake where the incident occurred. Avride is now evaluating technological improvements through controlled experiments to prevent similar situations while ensuring safety performance remains unaffected. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Multiple autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, currently operate in Austin.
